findings.title: Undo equal-timestamp answers in reverse log order
findings.problem: replayOrdered sorts redoRows only by descending at. JavaScript's stable sort leaves equal-timestamp answers in their original, forward order, but undoAbility must invert updates in reverse order. Elo updates are not commutative, so undoing a correct answer and an incorrect answer in forward order produces a different starting theta. The subsequent replay then saves an incorrect ability estimate.
findings.failure_scenario: A saved baseline contains two Pharmacology answers with the same millisecond timestamp, one correct and one incorrect. This is plausible when exam results call record repeatedly in one synchronous batch. Another device supplies an earlier answer, causing both baseline answers to be undone and replayed. The merged ability differs from applying the merged answer history in order, affecting readiness and adaptive selection.
findings.fix: Retain each baseline row's original ordinal and undo in reverse original application order, including timestamp ties. Use that ordinal when determining the history preceding each undone answer rather than excluding every equal-timestamp row with a strict timestamp comparison. Add a regression comparing merged ability against an in-order reference with tied timestamps.

findings.title: The revision guard silently drops saves from already-open clients
findings.problem: The previously shipped store adapter upserts progress without advancing revision and does not inspect Supabase's returned error. This trigger rejects every such update. Nothing in this change tells those already-running clients that saving has stopped or requires them to upgrade.
findings.failure_scenario: A student leaves the current app open across deployment, then studies another round. Every autosave receives the revision-conflict error, but the old adapter resolves normally and the screen continues as though progress were saved. Reloading loses all answers, XP, and scheduling changes made since deployment.
findings.fix: Provide a compatibility path for revisionless writes that preserves progress, or use a staged upgrade protocol that safely retires old clients before enforcing this trigger. Test a request made by the actual pre-change adapter against the migrated database, including what the student sees when the write is rejected.

findings.title: Question-only reconciliation can permanently discard an earned shift cover
findings.problem: mergeRewards uses the card-duplication heuristic to decide whether to include the server's cover delta. With unchanged SRS maps and no extra card XP, duplicate is true even when only the server earned a weekly cover. The server's cover is omitted, while its coverWeeks marker is retained, preventing the cover from ever being granted again.
findings.failure_scenario: Two devices load a baseline with four completed shifts and seven questions on Friday. Device A answers Friday's eighth question and banks a cover. Device B, still holding the baseline, changes its theme and encounters a revision conflict. Reconciliation replays A's question but does not run maybeGrantCover; duplicate is true, so the merged balance becomes zero covers while coverWeeks says Friday's week was already rewarded. A's earned protection is lost.
findings.fix: Reconcile weekly cover grants from their unique coverWeeks identities, independently of card-operation duplication, and reconcile consumption from the ordered activity history. Add a conflict test where the server earned a cover and the local device only changed a preference.

findings.title: Merging partial new-card ledgers erases the legacy daily count
findings.problem: mergeFcNew replaces count with ids.length whenever any side has an ids array. A valid legacy ledger can contain a nonzero count without ids, and noteNewCard preserves that count while adding only newly introduced IDs. Those IDs therefore do not represent the whole day's count.
findings.failure_scenario: Both devices load the supported legacy value { day: today, count: 12 }. Each introduces a different new card, producing count 13 with ids ["cA"] and count 13 with ids ["cB"]. A conflict merge returns count 2 instead of 14. The student is then allowed 18 more new cards rather than six, defeating the persisted daily cap.
findings.fix: Preserve the baseline's anonymous count and merge only the identified additions and removals relative to it. Do not treat a newly created ids array as a complete historical ledger. Add a regression using a nonzero baseline count with no ids and concurrent introductions.

assessment: Do not release yet. The new reconciliation code can alter ability estimates, discard earned shift covers, and reset legacy new-card counts. The revision guard also silently disables saving in already-open versions of the shipped app. The supplied tests do not exercise these failure paths.
